positions.as_written: Read a sectioning study's cutting order before its conclusion, because the order constrains what can be attributed.
Read posterior translation figures with their flexion angle attached, and discard any quoted without one.
Treat the double bundle question as open and read new work for whether its comparator is a well done single bundle procedure.
Read the gait work alongside the cadaveric work, since it is the only evidence here about a knee that is alive and loaded.
Take the patient's age and physiology into account, because the degeneration argument has decades to act in a young patient and may not in an older one.
Take their comorbidities into account, since this is a long and demanding rehabilitation.
Take the demands on their knee into account, because posterior instability declares itself on stairs and descending slopes rather than in a straight line.
Take their psychological state into account, since a knee that feels unreliable produces guarding that outlasts the ligament.
Record the balance and what tipped it, since the literature will not tip it.
Read the combined injury literature first, because recognising the corner changes management more than any decision about the PCL itself.
